newsitem.title: USA: Bio-Vascular sees Q3 revenues below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Bio-Vascular sees Q3 revenues below expectations.

text.p: Bio-Vascular Inc said it expects revenues for the third quarter ended July 31 to be lower than expected and future periods are likely to be affected, as well.
Expenses in the period will be higher than budgeted as a result of one-time costs related to the resignation of the company's former president and chief executive John Karcanes, the company said.

Third quareter revenues and revenues in future periods will likely be hurt by a delay in the start of a study of lung volume reduction surgery, a treatment for late-stage emphusema, which utlizes the company's Peri-Strips Dry product, the company said.

Revenue potential in the United States for the product has been reduced becasue the Health Care Financing Administration, which administers Medicare, has decided not to cover the surgery, the company said.

Bio-Vascular chief executive officer M. Karen Gilles said revenue from the Tissue-Guard product line, exclusive of Peri-Strips, continued to grow as expected in the third quarter, up 46 percent over the third quarter of 1996 and up 17 percent from the second quarter of 1997.

"We expect all Tissue-Guard markets to continue to grow," Gilles said. "However, the time frames for regulatory and reimbursement issues are under government control and are difficult to predict. We will diligently continue to pursue resolution of these issues."
Bio-Vascular shares were down 3/8 at 4-3/8 Thursday.
